title: DOE selects first companies for nuclear launch pad -- ANS / Nuclear Newswire
key_facts: The US Energy Department's Office of Nuclear Energy and the National Reactor Innovation Center (NRIC) announced the first four selections for the Nuclear Energy Launch Pad.
Three companies develop microreactors and one develops fuel supply: Deployable Energy, General Matter, NuCube Energy and Radiant Industries.
They were picked from applicants to the earlier Reactor Pilot Program and Fuel Line Pilot Program.
Inclusion lets them begin talks with NRIC on technical, regulatory and deployment support.
NRIC Director Brad Tomer said the launch pad widens the scope beyond reactor and fuel technologies.
quote_evidence: The Department of Energy's Office of Nuclear Energy and the National Reactor Innovation Center have announced their first selections for the Nuclear Energy Launch Pad: three companies developing microreactors and one developing fuel supply.

According to the DOE, inclusion in the program allows these companies to begin discussion with NRIC on the enhanced technical, regulatory, and deployment support that the Nuclear Energy Launch Pad can provide.
why_it_matters_hint: The government is lining up small reactors that could one day power remote sites and data centers, but selection promises support, not funding or a finished reactor.
notes: Announcement date not given in the text read; article published 15 Oct per the feed.
